headline: Flight chaos, a Microsoft outage and a fight over Brampton's auto plant
summary: Two technology failures hit daily life: a Microsoft outage that cut email at Toronto hospitals and a U.S. air traffic breakdown that cancelled thousands of flights and is now a funding fight in Washington. Ottawa moved against Stellantis over the sale of its Brampton plant while Carney tied any U.S. trade deal to autos. Abroad, the Strait of Hormuz stayed largely shut, and late U.S. election calls widened Democrats' gains.

top.headline: Hormuz stays mined and blockaded; Iran claims drone attacks on U.S. assets in Bahrain
top.what: Iran twice claimed drone attacks on a U.S. radar in Bahrain and reported tankers hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, none independently confirmed; U.S. forces said they shot down drones on Friday. Oil still fell for a second week, with Brent near US$96, as traders focused on ample supply.
top.why: The strait's closure is the main force behind high fuel prices and the inflation that has central banks raising rates.

top.headline: Nationwide FAA ground stop cancels thousands of flights, including Toronto's U.S. routes
top.what: A network failure on Friday halted every U.S. departure for more than four hours, and over 16,000 flights were cancelled across three days, including about 250 at Air Canada on Friday alone. President Trump and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy are now pressing Congress for up to US$50 billion to rebuild the system.
top.why: It stranded GTA travellers on cross-border routes and exposed how fragile U.S. air traffic control equipment is.

top.headline: Ottawa starts 30-day default clock on Stellantis over Brampton plant sale
top.what: After Stellantis finalized the sale of its idled Brampton assembly plant to armoured-vehicle maker Roshel, Ottawa declared the automaker in default of its subsidy agreement, and federal and Ontario ministers prepared a package to put to the company's global chief executive.
top.why: Thousands of laid-off Brampton auto workers and up to $529 million in public commitments are at stake.

top.headline: Carney says U.S. trade deal is closer but autos are a red line
top.what: Prime Minister Mark Carney said in Manila that talks with Washington are progressing but that he will not sign a deal that leaves Canada's auto sector unviable. He also closed free-trade talks with the Philippines.
top.why: Tariffs on autos and steel are the biggest threat to Ontario manufacturing jobs, with new vehicle tariffs threatened for January.

top.headline: Late calls extend Democratic gains; Alaska Senate race still open
top.what: Late calls went Democrats' way in Mississippi, in Kansas's governor's race and in Alaska's governor's race, while Democrat Mary Peltola sits just under 50% in Alaska's uncalled Senate contest ahead of a Nov. 18 ranked-choice count.
top.why: A larger Democratic majority in Congress from January shapes U.S. policy on tariffs, spending and oversight of the Trump administration.

top.headline: Nvidia scandal topples Huang and puts Commerce Secretary Lutnick under pressure
top.what: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang stepped down amid a scandal over chip sales to a China-linked buyer, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces criticism from both parties over delayed export curbs. The White House says Trump still has confidence in him.
top.why: Nvidia is one of the most widely held stocks in Canadian retirement and index funds, and the affair touches U.S. export controls on China.

top.headline: Microsoft outage knocks out email at Toronto hospitals, schools and governments
top.what: A Microsoft outage cut email and Teams at Toronto hospital networks and other public bodies before the company said service was fully restored on Saturday.
top.why: It showed how much hospitals and public services rely on a single company's online systems.

top.headline: Ukraine talks end without a land deal; Zelenskyy says U.S. floated Donbas-for-NATO swap
top.what: U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a breakthrough, and Ukraine's president said negotiators asked whether Kyiv would leave Donbas in return for NATO membership, which Washington has not confirmed. Russian and Ukrainian air attacks continued through the weekend.
top.why: Any settlement would reshape European security and Canada's NATO and aid commitments.
